text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — goldset evals for the new llama-3-compat quant build just dropped overall QA from 98.7% -> 95.2% on the factuality metric. Noticed right after the tokenizer patch landed.
Darren O'Neill: ugh. which tokenizer patch? PR link?
Maya Chen: https://git.internal/redwood/rl-tokenizer/pull/412 — small change to unicode normalization (NFKC) to reduce token splits.
Eli Torres: that's surprising, NFKC should be neutral. Is this on the main goldset or the smaller smoke set?
Maya Chen: main goldset (12k examples). CI alert popped at 12:40 UTC. `ci-bot` ran the full eval: see logs below.
ci-bot: Full eval job started: job/ev-2134567890, coverage=100%, model=llama3-q4
ci-bot: Metrics snapshot: factuality_mean=0.952 (prev=0.987), rougeL=0.612 (prev=0.618)
Sara K.: I can reproduce locally against the goldset with the same commit. Quick diff shows tokenizer produced different token counts for ~1.4k cases.
Pranay Rao: can we narrow to examples where tokenization changed? grep for tokens length delta > 0 and run eval on that subset.
Eli Torres: try `python -m eval_harness.slicer --filter token_delta --min 1 --out /tmp/delta.json` — that'll spit indices.
Maya Chen: ran that. delta subset ~1,412 examples. Ran eval on those: factuality drop is concentrated there (0.45 -> 0.12).
Darren O'Neill: interesting. Could be a subtle detokenization mismatch causing alignment errors in scoring. We score on string-match after detok? confirm.
Sara K.: scoring pipeline: detok -> normalize whitespace -> compare normalized spans. If detok uses different Unicode composition, match breaks.
Pranay Rao: hypothesis: NFKC changed composed/separated forms, scoring normalizer expects NFC. Quick fix: change scoring normalizer to NFKC to match tokenizer or revert tokenizer change.
Maya Chen: which direction is safer for production? We have enterprise customers relying on existing outputs.
Eli Torres: safer to make scorer tolerant first (accept both). Add NFKC normalize step and fallback to NFC if failure. Low-risk patch.
Darren O'Neill: agreed. Can we do a targeted patch to eval scoring lib and re-run goldset before touching tokenizer?
Maya Chen: I'll open PR to scoring: `eval-harness/patches/allow-nfkc` and include test vectors. ETA 1h.
ci-bot: Test run queued: job/ev-2134567901 (scoring-nfkc). Unit tests + goldset quick-run.
ops-bot: FYI deployment window for scoring libs is 01:00 UTC. We can hotfix to CI test runners without cluster rollout.
Sara K.: local quick-run with scoring-nfkc shows factuality moves back to 0.985 on goldset subset.
Pranay Rao: good sign. We should still audit tokenizer change; maybe it introduced token id mapping drift that affects caching later.
Maya Chen: filing an investigation ticket and tagging tokenizer owner @jules. Ticket: INTL-2389 — tokenizer normalization impact analysis.
Darren O'Neill: once scoring patch merges, let's re-run full goldset and run the model-canary against 3 customer-like workloads.
Eli Torres: also suggest adding a small evaluation check in the tokenizer PR gating: run `eval_harness --goldset-sanity` which compares metrics delta threshold < 0.5% for critical metrics.
Maya Chen: agreed — I'll add that as a gating check to the token PR pipeline.
Sara K.: note: there are ~60 examples where token counts increased by >8 and those will need human review. Pushing a CSV to the ticket.
ci-bot: job/ev-2134567901 completed: unit-tests=ok, goldset-quick=pass (factuality=0.986). Full goldset re-run scheduled.
Maya Chen: thanks all. Plan: (1) merge scoring-nfkc into eval-harness (hotfix to CI runners), (2) re-run full goldset, (3) hold tokenizer PR until INTL-2389 completes, (4) add gating check. Will update here.
Pranay Rao: and follow-up: check KV cache/key alignment for the quant runtime after tokenizer changes — add to INTL-2389 checklist.
Darren O'Neill: assign me for the canary runs.
Maya Chen: done — assigning. Closing slack thread once full goldset + canary complete.
